briefs.headline: Hannan draws 2-2 at Logan for its first tie of the season
briefs.summary: Hannan is 4-5-1 after Tuesday's 6:30 p.m. match in Logan, per the MaxPreps box score; no scorers were entered. Logan is 3-15-1. St. Mary's visits Ashton Thursday at 6 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Isak, Gakpo and Szoboszlai miss Liverpool's trip to LASK
briefs.summary: All three were hurt on international duty and are not in the 23-man party for Wednesday's Champions League match in Linz, 12:45 p.m. ET. Andoni Iraola said Tuesday he does not know when they return; Liverpool play four games in 10 days.

briefs.headline: Richarlison scores for Tottenham's under-21s at Cheltenham
briefs.summary: Left out of Spurs' 25-man Premier League squad, Richarlison scored in a draw at Cheltenham and converted in the shootout, which Spurs lost, Tuesday in the Jersey Mike's Trophy. He has not played for the first team since Aug. 22.

briefs.headline: Bengals tight end Hudson out for the season with a torn pectoral
briefs.summary: Tanner Hudson, who caught a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 win at Miami, tore the muscle making a special-teams tackle, his agent told ESPN Tuesday. Cincinnati claimed linebacker Jack Kiser off waivers Monday and put Swayze Bozeman on IR.

briefs.headline: Browns sign running back Estime, put Raheim Sanders on IR
briefs.summary: Audric Estime joins from Minnesota's practice squad after Sanders hurt a hip at the Jets, the club said Tuesday. Cleveland is 21st in rushing at 94.2 yards a game and Quinshon Judkins averages 3.0 a carry, per ESPN. Ravens visit Sunday.

briefs.headline: Crew sign Crew 2 forward Gbamble to a first-team contract
briefs.summary: Kevin Gbamble, who had 12 goals and 11 assists in MLS Next Pro this year, signed through June 2029; Columbus waived Cole Mrowka and bought an international slot from Portland for $75,000. Charlotte visits Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati open three-game homestand against New England
briefs.summary: Wednesday's 7:30 p.m. ET match is Cincinnati's first at TQL Stadium since Sept. 12; the club has won seven and lost two of 12 at home and is ninth in the East on 36 points. 'Winning is important at this stage,' Pat Noonan said Monday.

briefs.headline: Gibson says no Marshall job is secure after six-turnover loss
briefs.summary: 'Nobody's job is secure right now,' Tony Gibson said after Saturday's 27-21 loss to Coastal Carolina, WV MetroNews reported Tuesday. Judah Price ran 12 times for 124 yards; Zion Turner relieved Carlos Del Rio-Wilson, who threw three picks.

briefs.headline: Ohio visits Sacramento State in the schools' first meeting
briefs.summary: The Bobcats, unbeaten in two MAC games, kick off at 10 p.m. ET Saturday on ESPN+ against the Hornets, who have one win in six in their first FBS season and lost by 28 at Bowling Green last week, the school said Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez says WVU is reviewing everything on defense
briefs.summary: West Virginia has allowed an average of 46 points and 552 yards in its three Big 12 losses, 8.6 yards a play; the staff watched film for 4 1/2 hours Sunday, Rich Rodriguez said. Cincinnati visits at noon ET Saturday on TNT for homecoming.

briefs.headline: Peralta, Rays beat Guardians 3-1 to even the ALCS at 1-1
briefs.summary: Freddy Peralta threw six four-hit innings Tuesday in St. Petersburg; Liam Hicks' two-run single followed Jose Ramirez's error, and all three runs off Parker Messick were unearned. Game 3 is Thursday in Cleveland.

briefs.headline: Ohtani stays in the Dodgers' lineup for NLCS Game 3 tonight
briefs.summary: Dave Roberts said Tuesday that Ohtani was "adamant that he can help us"; he is 3 for 20 in the playoffs and has not homered since Aug. 18. Milwaukee leads the series two games to none; Robert Gasser faces Blake Snell at 8 p.m. ET on FS1.

briefs.headline: Mariners get permission to interview Astros manager Espada
briefs.summary: ESPN reported Tuesday, citing a source, that Seattle may talk to Joe Espada, whose Houston contract runs through October; he has 256 wins and 229 losses in three seasons. The Mariners fired Dan Wilson after an 86-loss season.

briefs.headline: Tkachuk brothers carry Panthers past Blue Jackets 7-3
briefs.summary: Brady Tkachuk scored three times in the second period Tuesday in Columbus and Matthew assisted on all three, tying a club record with five assists; Sam Reinhart's 86th power-play goal set a Florida record.

briefs.headline: Flyers fall to Kraken 3-2 in shootout, winless start hits 8
briefs.summary: Bobby McMann scored in regulation and in the fifth round of the shootout Tuesday in Philadelphia; the Flyers are 0-5-3, the longest winless start in franchise history, and share the league's winless list with the 0-3-2 Kings.

briefs.headline: Oilers beat Kings 4-1 behind McDavid for a 5th straight win
briefs.summary: Connor McDavid had a goal and two assists in the first period Tuesday in Los Angeles and has 16 points in six games; Devon Levi stopped 39 shots. Edmonton is 5-0-1 without Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins; the Kings are 0-3-2.

briefs.headline: Jury finds Hill liable on 2 of 10 counts, awards wife $500K
briefs.summary: A Miami jury found Tyreek Hill liable Tuesday for two counts of battery and not liable on eight other claims by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro; it denied punitive damages, and the NFL said the allegations remain under review.

briefs.headline: NFL suspends Bears' Montez Sweat 2 games under PED policy
briefs.summary: Sweat, 30, who led Chicago with 10 sacks last season, misses games at Atlanta and against New England and is eligible to return Oct. 23; the Bears activated Shemar Turner from the PUP list to take his roster spot.

briefs.headline: Greenlaw loses appeal, sits out 49ers' Monday night game
briefs.summary: Hearing officer James Thrash upheld the one-game suspension Tuesday for a late hit on Sam Darnold and a head-butt of helmetless Ernest Jones IV in Sunday's win in Seattle; rookie Jaden Dugger is likely to start against Washington.

briefs.headline: Florida State dismisses top recruit Kennon after arrest
briefs.summary: Freshman cornerback Chuck Kennon, No. 56 in the ESPN 300, was charged in Hillsborough County with felony fleeing to elude and false imprisonment over a Sunday incident; the school cited conduct detrimental to the team.

briefs.headline: Zverev edges Bublik in two tiebreaks in Shanghai round of 16
briefs.summary: The new year-end No. 1 won 7-6 (8-6), 4-6, 7-6 (7-1) Tuesday and faces Alex de Minaur in Thursday's quarterfinals; Casper Ruud advanced Wednesday when Felix Auger-Aliassime retired trailing 5-2 in the first set.

briefs.headline: Asasuiryu joins the autumn tour after a fractured eye socket
briefs.summary: He joined the jungyo (regional tour) Tuesday at Kahoku, Ishikawa, after fracturing the inner wall of his left eye socket on Day 5 of the September basho (tournament), his top-division debut; he needs no surgery.

briefs.headline: Onosato drills a top-division newcomer at the Kahoku stop
briefs.summary: The yokozuna (grand champion) gave a 26-year-old Isegahama stable wrestler, new to the top division in September, four minutes of butsukari (pushing drills) Tuesday on the jungyo (regional tour); the newcomer said he needs more weight.

coming_in.item: One day out. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:38 a.m., makes the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, seven days a week, by hand and hand-operated implements only; it is unlawful to possess oysters under three inches shell length, to take oysters between sunset and sunrise, or to take them from the oyster sanctuaries listed in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:38 a.m. and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, still reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

sections.label: On the Water
sections.note: All four waters reported from the locked fishing.json, generated_at 2026-10-14T05:32:25-04:00, errors list empty; the file was not re-run by this desk and every figure is printed as it stands there. The Williams River is on its third day of recession from Sunday's blowout: 451 cfs and 2.80 feet at 5:15 a.m. against 797 cfs and 3.47 feet at 5:15 a.m. Tuesday, the true 24-hour mark and Tuesday's edition reading, on a USGS 03186500 two-day trace pulled at 5:36 a.m., so the river is FALLING on the day, down 346 cfs and 0.67 feet, and the fetcher's falling flags are right. Its comparison points are not 24-hour marks: the 1,370 cfs and 4.28 feet in its 24h_ago fields are the first point of its two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Monday reading, 47.5 hours before the current one, the same window-start bug as the last three mornings, and against them the fall reads as 919 cfs and 1.48 feet instead of 346 and 0.67; the direction happens to be right today because the river has fallen every hour since Monday's 9 a.m. secondary crest. The trace hour by hour: 1,550 cfs and 4.51 feet at 9 a.m. Monday, the window high, 1,220 at 5 p.m., 943 at midnight, 797 at 5 and 5:15 a.m. Tuesday, then 767 at 6, 750 at 7, 726 at 8, 704 at 9, 693 at 10, 676 at 11, 654 at noon, 644 at 1 p.m., 628 at 2, 617 at 3, 597 at 4, 582 at 5, 567 at 6, 557 at 7, 542 at 8, 533 at 9, 523 at 10, 509 at 11, 495 at midnight, 491 at 1 a.m., 477 at 2, 468 at 3, 459 at 4, 451 at 5 and 5:15 a.m.; the hourly steps ran 17 to 30 cfs Tuesday morning, 10 to 20 through the afternoon and evening, and 4 to 14 overnight, 8 in the last hour. Wadeable at the edges, not across.", and the direction is right this morning, though the comparison still is not a 24-hour mark: the 1,370 cfs and 4.28 feet in the fetcher's 24h_ago fields are the first point of its two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Monday reading, and the USGS 03186500 trace pulled at 5:36 a.m. puts the true 24-hour mark at 797 cfs and 3.47 feet at 5:15 a.m. Tuesday, Tuesday's edition reading, so the river is down 346 cfs and 0.67 feet on the day, not 919 and 1.48. The same water is draining out of the Gauley: the Craigsville gauge above Summersville Lake (03189100) read 1,780 cfs and 12.40 feet at 4:30 a.m. against 3,050 at 5 a.m. Tuesday and the 4,250 peak of Monday afternoon; 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, dropped from 11.04 feet at 2 a.m. Tuesday to 7.73 by 9 a.m., held there to 7 p.m., came back up to 9.12 at 9 p.m. and has held 9.12 since, a cut and a partial restoration at the dam read off a USGS stage trace and not a Corps statement; and the Gauley above Belva (03192000) fell from 3,980 cfs at 5 a.m. Tuesday to a low of 1,300 at 3:45 to 4:15 a.m. and then read 1,320, 1,370 and 1,450 cfs at 4:30, 4:45 and 5 a.m., the evening increase at the dam arriving. NWS's active product list for West Virginia was empty at 5:36 a.m., no flood watch, warning or advisory on the Gauley, Elk or Williams. At 451 cfs and falling this is the heavy-nymph-on-the-seam river, not the long-leader one: the water is still carrying color and pushing through the pocket water, so the fish that are feeding are on the inside seams and the soft edges, which is also the only water the fetcher calls wadeable. Stoneflies and caddis are the forage, so a weighted size 8 stonefly nymph on point with a size 14 caddis pupa on a dropper, enough split shot to tick bottom, fished under an indicator up the inside seam of each run and into the eddies below the plunge pools from the near bank; a sculpin is the other forage in the file, so an olive or black sculpin streamer on a sink-tip, cast tight to the undercut banks and swung slow through the tailouts of the plunge pools, covers the fish the nymph rig cannot reach without wading across, which the fetcher's read says not to do. WVDNR's trout stocking page was not opened today; no stocking line is printed. Sept. 22-23's high water took 19 days to recede to base flow; at 8 cfs an hour this one is a week or more from the clear-water, long-leader river, and the trace will say when.

waters.working: Fourth day past the new moon: the fetcher's file carries the moon as a waxing crescent, 10 percent lit and 3.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:38 a.m., puts the new moon at 15:50 UT Saturday, Oct. 10, the first quarter at 16:12 UT Sunday, Oct. 18, and the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26, so the spring tides are still on but easing toward Sunday's neap: the surf swing has come down from 5.3 feet Monday and 5.0 Tuesday to 4.6 today. NWS Wilmington had no product for Coastal Pender at 5:36 a.m., no rip current statement, no high surf advisory, no coastal flood advisory, the third quiet beach morning in a row. The sound at Hampstead came off a 0.7-foot low at 5:11 a.m., already past at press time, and fills 3.5 feet to a 4.2-foot high at 11:28 a.m.; it then drains 3.1 feet to a 1.1-foot low at 5:58 p.m., so the last two hours of the ebb, about 4 to 5:58 p.m., land in the late afternoon, and fills 2.2 feet to a 3.3-foot high at 11:44 p.m., after dark; all four sound events fall inside Wednesday. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 3:45 a.m. at 0.6, high 10:22 a.m. at 5.2, low 4:51 p.m. at 0.8, high 10:39 p.m. at 3.8, a 4.6- and 4.4-foot swing against Tuesday's 5.0 and 4.8. Today's lags from the two tables are 66 and 65 minutes on the highs and 86 and 67 minutes on the lows, against 61 and 59 and 87 and 70 on Tuesday; the morning low again lags longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 75.6 degrees at 5:24 a.m., up 1.1 from Tuesday's 74.5 and the warmest reading since the weekend. What is running is 13 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:36 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings starting to show at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered through the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, a few trout on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jrs. and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds on shrimp at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under diving birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait everywhere, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem: the 11:28 a.m. high puts 4.2 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, which is where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 9:30 to 11:28 a.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the ebb, roughly 4 to 5:58 p.m., a daylight ebb an hour later than Tuesday's with no beach product over it: finger mullet and shrimp are the forage and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead; on the evening flood, 5:58 to 11:44 p.m., a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they cover, and the dock lights are the trout spot after the thin crescent sets, though with the water at Beaufort up to 75.6 the cool-down the report says the trout are waiting on has not come. The surf side, with no advisory on it and 5.2 feet of water at the pier on the 10:22 a.m. high, is Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs for the Spanish and bluefish on the morning flood and cut bait on the bottom for the slot reds in the evening, the pattern every pier in the report gives. Slack at 11:28 a.m., 5:58 p.m. and 11:44 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only.
